visual_review.notes: Final captures inspected after scenery residency; supported intended positions and zero deaths asserted. Main lite recovery includes one deliberate fall.

limitations: The native main run is continuous and collects all 104 main/checkpoint boxes; it bypasses the linked bonus, so the 159-box gem correctly remains unearned.

Browser main traversal covers the continuous spawn-to-second-checkpoint prefix using per-physics-step controller input in the normal game loop, real fall recovery, and a separately staged keyboard walking finish. It is not a continuous browser all-box main run.

Full-render views use staged starts. The corrected return-gallery previews trigger their corresponding switches after reset, then assert the player remains on the 12.4 m floors; the continuous journeys separately prove reaching those switches. Initial captures activated only outline crates, leaving their floors absent, and were replaced.

The spent-TNT negative trial removes the support as fixture setup, then uses ordinary input to test the new retreat payload. It proves this tested bypass fails, not that every imaginable route is impossible.
The main audit records one crate touching a rail; forced-kite contact collects it successfully. No main crate is floating, over a void or overhanging.
Bonus audit floating/void warnings describe preserved relay markers and high tool rewards. Steel-arrow targets are receiving footings; a simple overhead-target audit labels two fruit-only or empty.
Native tests use fallback artwork and a fixed initial wind seed. Browser passes exercise the actual assets and check console errors separately.

The first bonus browser run stopped at the far sentry because its pilot context omitted TUNING, which the existing projectile-avoidance helper reads. The shared browser harness now supplies the game tuning; gameplay tuning is unchanged.

Preliminary frame-driven keyboard pilots collected 15 and 10 of 18 prefix boxes: software rendering caused coarse feedback and steering overshoot. The post-hop stack moved from z=232 to z=245 to allow lane settling. Final collection uses controller input sampled per physics step; recovery and finish checks are separate.

timing.notes: Main layout authoring took about ten minutes. Native route, bonus lost-support corrections, software browser validation and evidence packaging extended the pair beyond the requested 20-minute total. Browser steering revealed one additional post-hop stack correction.
